newsitem.title: USA: U.S. SPOT RESIDS HOLD AGAIN DESPITE SOFTER CRUDE.
newsitem.headline: U.S. SPOT RESIDS HOLD AGAIN DESPITE SOFTER CRUDE.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices mostly held steady again Wednesday in moderate activity, with further gains in East Coast city gate gas values underpinning the complex despite mild weather and softer crude.
"With gas still firm, I don't see resid slipping much even with demand slowing because of the weather," said one cash trader, noting firm high sulphur grades also helped prop up the market.

In New York Harbor, physical one percent held at about $16 a barrel, with August one percent paper done early at $16.30. September one percent paper was talked slightly lower at $16.20-50 with softer crude, while Q4 paper was rated at $16.80-17.05, traders said.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour remained firmly in the $18-plus area, helped by prospects for some utility stocking.
High sulphurs in New York also were steady, with 2.2 percent still at $14.75-15.00 though some pegged the number closer to $15 on firm bunkers.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices were stable to higher, with one percent still at $15.50-75, while three percent gained slightly to the low-$15s on strong bunkers.

New York city gate gas prices held fairly steady Wednesday in the low-$2.50s/mmBtu, or $15.94 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, firmed about five cents to the high-$2.30s/mmBtu, or about $14.99 a barrel.
